related_synthesis_entries.claim: The threshold 1/log T is simultaneously eigenangle resolution in the unitary model, the cutoff in prime-sum covariance, and the distance at which shifted zeta poles merge inside the lower-bound contour.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The upper bound replaces moments by tail probabilities of log zeta, whereas the lower bound replaces zeta powers by correlation with a short polynomial; both interfaces expose the same pairwise covariance product.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The upper route assumes RH and permits real exponents; the lower route is unconditional but uses positive integers and additional shift restrictions.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The squared norm of the resonator is encoded by a multiplicative Dirichlet series whose Euler product has zeta poles at every pairwise shift difference; a Perron contour turns geometric clustering of shifts into clustered residues.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The coefficient square D(j) is multiplicative, and its Dirichlet series factors into zeta functions at zero and at plus or minus pairwise shift differences times an analytic Euler product. A truncated Perron integral is moved through the corresponding poles to evaluate the resonator norm.
directed.conceptual_reading: An arithmetic norm is compressed into singularity data. Nearness among shifts becomes nearness among poles, making correlation geometry accessible to contour methods.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Euler factorization bridges coefficient convolution to a zeta-product; the Perron kernel bridges the partial sum to residues; a close-shift graph later organizes which poles should be enclosed together.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The contour analysis is formula-heavy, and the excerpt begins a proof whose suppression of nonleading residues continues in the next unit.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the pole-encoding architecture; exact Euler exponents and truncation errors should be checked.
